channel.description: poems and songs of the Kara-Buura · Jumabai ata

item.title: From the family
item.description: This is Cholpon. Our grandfather Jumabai Sydykov died on 11 September, at home, in his 80th year. He was buried the next day beside his father, under the apricot tree hill. He asked that the blog stay open, so that the poems are not lost with the notebook. Thank you to everyone who read him and…

item.title: New Year
item.description: Eleven grandchildren came, and three great-grandchildren. The house was too small and the dog was too happy. Cholpon says there are 900 readers of this blog in six years. I said: that is one aitysh crowd. Good.

item.title: Grandfather's apricot
item.description: My father planted it in the year of the famine, when nobody planted anything. The neighbours laughed: who will eat it? Eighty years they have eaten it. [photo: apricots | The tree this summer, still giving.]

item.title: Akyns' contest in Kyzyl-Adyr
item.description: The district held an aitysh in the square by the House of Culture, the first in eleven years. Two young akyns, a boy from Kyzyl-Adyr and a girl from the hill villages, improvised against each other for an hour. The girl won. The boy was very good also, but the girl made the district head laugh and…

item.title: The cold winter
item.description: The light comes two hours in the evening, we eat by it like by a fire. The children do lessons by the lamp. In 1943 the lamp was the same lamp. Cholpon says it is not nice to compare. But I am 74, I am allowed to compare.

item.title: Wedding song for Cholpon's sister
item.description: Her sister married a boy from Talas. At the toi I sang the old wedding song, the kerez of the bride, and the young people filmed it on their telephones. Now my voice is in the telephones in Talas. A strange world. Go, my bird, to the city of stone, take the mountain wind in your sleeve. When the…

item.title: For those who left
item.description: The gate is open, the dog does not bark, the samovar is cold on the shelf. Who closes a house like this, in a hurry, and leaves the door to the wind? Come back, neighbours. The apricots do not know there was a war. Written this spring. I will not say more.

item.title: The komuz of my teacher
item.description: My teacher of the komuz was blind Asanbek, who played at the House of Culture before me. He tuned by the sound of the river. When they built the new reservoir he said the river now plays in a different key, and he retuned all his songs. I still play them in his key. [photo: lake | The reservoir in…

item.title: Spring on the jailoo
item.description: The snow went off the pass on Tuesday, the horses knew it before the radio. My grandson laughs: grandfather, the radio is faster. I say: the radio has never smelled the grass. Written in May 1979 at the summer pasture above the valley. The grandson in the poem is now a grandfather himself, may God…

item.title: A word before the songs
item.description: Assalamu aleikum, readers. My granddaughter says now there are people in America who can read what an old man from the Kara-Buura writes. I don't believe her, but let it be. I have written songs since 1951. The best ones were sung at weddings and forgotten by morning, as it should be. The ones…
